overall_summary: High-performing shorts leverage 'What If' scenarios that visually transform the familiar Earth landscape. Videos referencing planetary scale changes (Earth/Saturn rings) or sudden, high-stakes physical reversals (losing atmosphere, changing speed of light) consistently drive higher engagement and longer viewing durations than more abstract phenomena.

what_is_working.evidence: Videos about Saturn-like rings on Earth (1,038 views) and atmospheric shifts consistently outperform.
what_is_working.action: Prioritize visual representations of Earth interacting with massive celestial structures or atmospheric colors.

what_is_working.evidence: Videos with specific, short-duration event triggers perform significantly better in retention metrics.
what_is_working.action: Maintain the '5-second' or '10-second' threshold in titles and scripts to trigger high-curiosity, low-commitment viewing.

what_to_improve.evidence: Retention curves drop significantly (often below 30%) within the first 5 seconds of abstract content.
what_to_improve.action: Eliminate preambles; start the video mid-event with the core visual change occurring at 0:00.

what_to_improve.evidence: Average sub conversion remains stagnant across most high-view content.
what_to_improve.action: Add a hard, visual Call-to-Action (CTA) at the 50% watch mark, not at the end, where retention curves often plateau.

retention_insights.evidence: High relative retention at 49% progress indicates viewers wait for the 'reset' or explanation.
retention_insights.action: Ensure the payoff (the scientific outcome of the event) hits precisely at the 50% mark of the total length.

best_posting_windows.reason: Successful peaks observed around 04:55-05:05 UTC; captures early European and Asian audiences.
Multiple high-performing uploads (e.g., Asteroids, Earth/Venus orbit swap) clustered here.
